stem: Write the molecular formula and structural formula of BHA and BHT. What are thermoplastic polymers?
solution:
**BHA — butylated hydroxyanisole.**

Molecular formula : \(\mathrm{C_{11}H_{16}O_2}\)

Structural formula : it is tert-butyl-4-methoxyphenol, a phenol ring carrying a methoxy group and a tert-butyl group on the ring —

\(\mathrm{HO-C_6H_3(OCH_3)-C(CH_3)_3}\)

**BHT — butylated hydroxytoluene.**

Molecular formula : \(\mathrm{C_{15}H_{24}O}\)

Structural formula : it is 2,6-di-tert-butyl-4-methylphenol, a phenol ring carrying tert-butyl groups at positions 2 and 6 and a methyl group at position 4 —

\(\mathrm{HO-C_6H_2(C(CH_3)_3)_2-CH_3}\)

Both are phenolic antioxidants added to fats and oils. The phenolic \(\mathrm{-OH}\) hands a hydrogen atom to the chain-carrying peroxy radical and so breaks the oxidation chain.

**Thermoplastic polymers.**

Plasticity is the property of being easily shaped or moulded, and thermoplastic polymers are the polymers that are capable of **repeated softening on heating and hardening on cooling**, so that they can be moulded again and again.

The reason lies in the forces between the chains. Their chains are linear or lightly branched and carry **no cross links**, and the intermolecular forces holding them are only moderately strong — intermediate between the weak van der Waals forces of an elastomer and the hydrogen bonding of a fibre. On heating the chains therefore slide past one another and the solid softens; on cooling the same forces lock them again and it hardens.

Examples : polythene, polystyrene, polyvinyls, PET.

stem: Explain with examples, branched and linear polymers.
solution:
Polymers are classified on the basis of **structure**, that is the chain configuration — the way the monomer units are linked together. Which arrangement is obtained depends on the nature and the number of functional groups present in the monomer.

**Linear (straight chain) polymers.** The monomer molecules are joined one after another in a single linear arrangement, with no side chains. They are obtained from bifunctional monomers or from alkenes. Because the chains are unbranched they lie close to one another, the intermolecular forces act along the whole length of the chain and the polymer is closely packed. Such polymers therefore have **high density** and high melting point and tensile strength.

Examples : high density polythene, PVC, nylon 6,6, terylene.

**Branched chain polymers.** Here a long main chain carries side chains growing out of it. They are obtained from a monomer having three functional groups, or from a monomer already carrying side chains. The branches keep the main chains apart, so the chains are loosely held and cannot pack regularly. Such polymers therefore have **low density** and a lower melting point and tensile strength.

Examples : low density polythene, glycogen, amylopectin.

Polythene shows the contrast in one substance : the same polymer \(\mathrm{[CH_2-CH_2]_n}\) is dense and stiff when the chains grow linear (HDP) and light and flexible when H-atom abstraction during the polymerization introduces branches (LDP).

stem: What are biodegradable polymers and non-biodegradable polymers? Write one example of each. Explain cationic detergents
solution:
**Biodegradable polymers.** Polymers that are attacked and broken down by the micro-organisms present in the environment, so that after use they degrade to simple harmless products instead of accumulating as waste. Their chains carry a large proportion of polar, hydrolysable linkages — ester or amide — like those in natural biopolymers such as proteins, and it is these linkages that the microbial enzymes attack. Aliphatic polyesters and aliphatic polyamides are the important classes.

Example : PHBV, poly(\(\beta\)-hydroxybutyrate-co-\(\beta\)-hydroxyvalerate), the aliphatic polyester copolymer of \(\beta\)-hydroxybutyric acid and \(\beta\)-hydroxyvaleric acid.

**Non-biodegradable polymers.** Polymers that are not affected by microbes. Most synthetic polymers are of this kind : their backbone is a chain of \(\mathrm{C-C}\) bonds carrying no hydrolysable group, so the enzymes have nothing to attack. Their waste therefore stays in the environment for a very long time and poses a pollution hazard.

Example : polythene, \(\mathrm{[CH_2-CH_2]_n}\).

**Cationic detergents.** Cationic detergents are quaternary ammonium salts of long chain amines, with chloride, bromide or acetate as the anion. The long hydrocarbon chain is the water-repelling part and the quaternary ammonium head is the water-loving part; since that head carries a **positive** charge, the surface-active part of the molecule is the **cation**, and that is what distinguishes a cationic detergent from an anionic one, whose surface-active part is the anion.

Example : cetyltrimethylammonium bromide,

\(\mathrm{[CH_3(CH_2)_{15}N(CH_3)_3]^{\oplus}\ Br^{\ominus}}\)

They also have germicidal properties, and are used in hair conditioners and in mouthwashes.

stem: Explain the following terms: \(\text{a}\). Homopolymers \(\text{b}\). Elastomers.
solution:
**a. Homopolymers.**

Homopolymers are the polymers which have **only one type of repeating unit**. Usually they are formed from a single monomer, and in some cases the one repeating unit is itself formed by the condensation of two distinct monomers.

\(n\,\mathrm{CH_2{=}CH_2} \xrightarrow{\text{polymerization}} \mathrm{[CH_2-CH_2]_n}\)

Here every unit along the chain is \(\mathrm{-CH_2-CH_2-}\), so polythene is a homopolymer.

Examples : polythene, polypropene, polyacrylonitrile, nylon 6, nylon 6,6.

A polymer having two or more types of repeating unit, formed from two or more different monomers polymerized in presence of each other, is a copolymer instead — Buna-S and Buna-N are the standard examples.

**b. Elastomers.**

Elasticity is the property by which a substance gets stretched by an external force and restores its original shape on release of that force. Elastomers are the elastic polymers, and they are one of the four classes into which polymers are placed on the basis of **intermolecular forces**.

The intermolecular forces in an elastomer are the **weakest** of the four, of the van der Waals type. They are weak because the chain is coiled and irregular, so it is only these short-range forces that hold neighbouring chains, and an applied force can therefore pull the coiled chains out and stretch the material. A **few cross links** between the chains stop the chains from sliding past one another permanently and pull the stretched polymer back to its original position when the force is removed, which is what makes the material elastic rather than merely soft.

Examples : vulcanised rubber, Buna-S, Buna-N, neoprene.

stem: Write classification of polymers on the basis of structure.
solution:
On the basis of **structure** — that is the chain configuration, the way the monomer units are linked together — polymers are classified into three general types. Which one is obtained depends on the nature and the number of functional groups present in the monomer.

| Type | How the chains are built | Monomer that gives it | Examples |
|---|---|---|---|
| Linear (straight chain) | monomer units joined one after another in a single linear arrangement, with no branches; the chains pack closely, so the polymer has high density and high melting point and tensile strength | bifunctional monomers, or alkenes | high density polythene, PVC |
| Branched chain | a long main chain carrying side chains; the branches keep the chains apart so they are loosely held, and the density is low | a monomer with three functional groups, or one already carrying side chains | low density polythene |
| Cross linked (network) | cross links are produced between the linear chains, tying them into a single rigid three dimensional network; the material is hard, insoluble and infusible | polyfunctional monomers | bakelite, melamine-formaldehyde resin |

The three classes therefore differ only in how many points on a monomer can join to a neighbour : two give a chain, three give a branch, and more than that ties the chains to one another.

stem: Define: Non-biodegradable polymer. Write the preparation of terylene.
solution:
**Non-biodegradable polymer.** A non-biodegradable polymer is a polymer which is **not affected by the micro-organisms** present in the environment, so that its waste is not broken down and stays in the environment for a very long time, posing a pollution hazard. Most synthetic polymers are of this kind, because their backbone is a chain of \(\mathrm{C-C}\) bonds carrying no hydrolysable linkage for the microbial enzymes to attack.

Examples : polythene, PVC, polystyrene, teflon.

**Preparation of terylene.**

Terylene, also called dacron, is the commercially most important polyester fibre. It is prepared by the **condensation polymerization** of ethylene glycol with terephthalic acid, in presence of a zinc acetate-antimony trioxide catalyst at 420-460 K.

An alcoholic \(\mathrm{-OH}\) group of the glycol condenses with a \(\mathrm{-COOH}\) group of the acid, a molecule of water is eliminated and the **ester linkage** \(\mathrm{-CO-O-}\) is formed. Both monomers are bifunctional, so the same condensation repeats at both ends of every unit and a long chain results :

\(n\,\mathrm{HO-CH_2-CH_2-OH} + n\,\mathrm{HOOC-C_6H_4-COOH} \xrightarrow[-n\mathrm{H_2O}]{420-460\ \mathrm{K}} \mathrm{[O-CH_2-CH_2-O-CO-C_6H_4-CO]_n}\)

Because a small molecule is eliminated, the repeating unit does not have the same elemental composition as the monomers, which is the mark of a condensation polymer. Terylene melts at \(265\,^\circ\mathrm{C}\), is resistant to chemicals and water, and is blended with cotton and wool to make wrinkle-free fabrics.

stem: Mention the types of polymers formed on the basis of intermolecular forces.
solution:
The mechanical properties of a polymer — tensile strength, toughness, elasticity — depend on the forces acting between its chains. On the basis of **intermolecular forces** polymers are placed in four classes.

**1. Elastomers.** The intermolecular forces are the **weakest** of the four, of the van der Waals type, which permits the coiled chains to be stretched apart by an external force. A few cross links between the chains pull the stretched polymer back to its original shape once the force is removed.

Examples : vulcanised rubber, Buna-S, Buna-N, neoprene.

**2. Fibres.** The intermolecular forces are the **strongest** of the four — hydrogen bonding and strong dipole-dipole attraction. They hold the chains close and regular, so the solid is crystalline and has high tensile strength, that is resistance to breaking under tension, and can be drawn into threads.

Examples : polyamides such as nylon 6,6, polyesters such as terylene.

**3. Thermoplastic polymers.** The intermolecular forces are **moderately strong**, intermediate between those of elastomers and fibres, and there is no cross linking. The chains therefore slide past one another on heating and lock again on cooling, so the polymer softens repeatedly on heating and hardens on cooling and can be moulded again and again.

Examples : polythene, polystyrene, polyvinyls.

**4. Thermosetting polymers.** Here the chains are joined to one another by **extensive cross linking** through covalent bonds, formed in the mould during the hot setting process, giving a rigid three dimensional network. Once hardened the polymer becomes infusible : it cannot be softened by heating and cannot be remoulded.

Examples : bakelite, urea-formaldehyde resin, melamine-formaldehyde resin.

The order of the four is therefore an order of increasing restraint on the chains — van der Waals forces only, then hydrogen bonding, then no cross links but stronger forces, and finally covalent cross links throughout.

stem: How are polythene and neoprene prepared?
solution:
**Polythene.** Polythene, \(\mathrm{[CH_2-CH_2]_n}\), is prepared by the **addition polymerization** of ethylene. The monomer is unsaturated, so it simply adds and no small molecule is lost :

\(n\,\mathrm{CH_2{=}CH_2} \longrightarrow \mathrm{[CH_2-CH_2]_n}\)

The conditions decide which of its two kinds is obtained.

**Low density polythene (LDP)** : ethylene is polymerized under high pressure, 1000-2000 atm, at 350-570 K, in presence of traces of \(\mathrm{O_2}\) or a peroxide as initiator. The mechanism is free radical addition accompanied by **H-atom abstraction**, and it is that abstraction which introduces branching, so the chains are loosely held and the density is low.

**High density polythene (HDP)** : ethene is polymerized at 333-343 K and only 6-7 atm in presence of a **Ziegler-Natta catalyst**, a combination of triethyl aluminium with titanium tetrachloride. There is no H-atom abstraction, so the chain grows essentially linear, packs closely and the density is high.

**Neoprene.** Neoprene is the **addition polymer of chloroprene**, that is 2-chloro-1,3-butadiene. Chloroprene polymerizes rapidly in presence of oxygen. Both double bonds of the conjugated diene take part and a new double bond appears in the middle of every repeating unit :

\(n\,\mathrm{CH_2{=}C(Cl)-CH{=}CH_2} \xrightarrow{\text{polymerization}} \mathrm{[CH_2-C(Cl){=}CH-CH_2]_n}\)

Neoprene is vulcanized in presence of magnesium oxide.

Both are addition polymers, because in each case the monomer is unsaturated and adds without eliminating anything — polythene from a simple alkene, neoprene from a conjugated diene, which is why the neoprene chain retains one double bond per unit and can be vulcanized while polythene cannot.

stem: Explain the preparation and uses of \(\text{nylon-2-nylon-6}\).
solution:
**Preparation.**

Nylon 2-nylon 6 is a polyamide **copolymer** of two amino acids, namely glycine and \(\varepsilon\)-amino caproic acid :

glycine, \(\mathrm{H_2N-CH_2-COOH}\), and \(\varepsilon\)-amino caproic acid, \(\mathrm{H_2N-(CH_2)_5-COOH}\).

Each monomer is bifunctional, carrying one \(\mathrm{-COOH}\) group and one \(\mathrm{-NH_2}\) group. On heating, the \(\mathrm{-COOH}\) of one molecule condenses with the \(\mathrm{-NH_2}\) of the next, a molecule of water is eliminated at every step and the **amide linkage** \(\mathrm{-CO-NH-}\) is formed. This is condensation polymerization, and the two amino acids alternate along the chain :

\(n\,\mathrm{H_2N-CH_2-COOH} + n\,\mathrm{H_2N-(CH_2)_5-COOH} \xrightarrow{-n\mathrm{H_2O}} \mathrm{[NH-CH_2-CO-NH-(CH_2)_5-CO]_n}\)

The unit \(\mathrm{NH-CH_2-CO}\) comes from glycine, which has 2 carbon atoms, and the unit \(\mathrm{NH-(CH_2)_5-CO}\) from \(\varepsilon\)-amino caproic acid, which has 6. That is the origin of the numbers 2 and 6 in the name.

**Uses.**

Nylon 2-nylon 6 is a **biodegradable** polymer, and its use follows from that. The chain is an aliphatic polyamide carrying a large proportion of polar amide linkages — the very linkages that hold a protein together — so the enzymes of soil microbes can hydrolyse them and the article is degraded after use instead of remaining in the environment.

It is therefore used as a biodegradable plastic, in place of an ordinary non-biodegradable plastic in articles that are thrown away after use, so that the waste does not accumulate and pose a pollution hazard.

stem: Write chemical reactions to prepare the following polymers: (i) Teflon (ii) \(\text{Nylon-6}\) (iii) Dextron.
solution:
**(i) Teflon.**

Chemically teflon is polytetrafluoroethylene. Its monomer, tetrafluoroethylene \(\mathrm{CF_2{=}CF_2}\), is a gas at room temperature and is polymerized at high pressure using a free radical initiator such as hydrogen peroxide or ammonium persulphate. The monomer is unsaturated, so it adds and no small molecule is lost — **addition polymerization** :

\(n\,\mathrm{CF_2{=}CF_2} \xrightarrow[\text{high pressure}]{\text{peroxide}} \mathrm{[CF_2-CF_2]_n}\)

**(ii) Nylon 6.**

\(\varepsilon\)-Caprolactam is the cyclic amide, or lactam, \(\mathrm{-NH-CO-(CH_2)_5-}\), whose two ends are joined into a seven membered ring. On heating with water at 533-543 K the ring opens at the amide bond and one monomer unit at a time adds to the growing chain — **ring opening polymerization** — giving the polyamide nylon 6 :

\(n\,(\varepsilon\text{-caprolactam}) \xrightarrow[533-543\ \mathrm{K}]{\mathrm{H_2O}} \mathrm{[NH-(CH_2)_5-CO]_n}\)

Nothing is eliminated, so the repeating unit has the same elemental composition as the monomer. The name nylon 6 is given on the basis of the six carbon atoms present in the monomer unit.

**(iii) Dextron.**

Dextron is the biodegradable aliphatic polyester obtained by the **condensation polymerization** of glycolic acid, that is hydroxyacetic acid \(\mathrm{HO-CH_2-COOH}\). The molecule is bifunctional, carrying one \(\mathrm{-OH}\) group and one \(\mathrm{-COOH}\) group, so the \(\mathrm{-OH}\) of one molecule condenses with the \(\mathrm{-COOH}\) of the next, water is eliminated and the **ester linkage** \(\mathrm{-CO-O-}\) is formed :

\(n\,\mathrm{HO-CH_2-COOH} \xrightarrow{-n\mathrm{H_2O}} \mathrm{[O-CH_2-CO]_n}\)

Its chain is held together by hydrolysable ester linkages, which is why it is degraded in the body, and it is used for absorbable surgical sutures.

The three together cover the three modes of polymerization : teflon by addition of an unsaturated monomer, nylon 6 by the opening of a ring, and dextron by condensation of a difunctional monomer with loss of water.

stem: Write the reactions for the formation of nylon \(6,6\) polymer.
solution:
Nylon 6,6 is a **polyamide** — the inter-unit linkage is \(\mathrm{-CO-NH-}\) — obtained from the two bifunctional monomers **adipic acid** and **hexamethylenediamine**. It is formed in two steps.

**Step 1 — salt formation.** Adipic acid and hexamethylenediamine are mixed. The acid protonates the diamine and the **nylon salt**, hexamethylene diammonium adipate, separates :

\(\mathrm{HOOC-(CH_2)_4-COOH} + \mathrm{H_2N-(CH_2)_6-NH_2} \longrightarrow \mathrm{{}^{-}O-CO-(CH_2)_4-CO-O^{-}}\ \mathrm{{}^{+}H_3N-(CH_2)_6-NH_3^{+}}\)

**Step 2 — condensation polymerization.** The nylon salt is heated to about 553 K under high pressure. Each \(\mathrm{-COOH}\) group condenses with an \(\mathrm{-NH_2}\) group, a molecule of water is eliminated at every linkage and the amide bond is formed :

\(n\,(\text{nylon salt}) \xrightarrow[-n\mathrm{H_2O}]{553\ \mathrm{K},\ \text{high pressure}} \mathrm{[CO-(CH_2)_4-CO-NH-(CH_2)_6-NH]_n}\)

The product is the polyamide fibre nylon 6,6. The two numerals stand for the six carbon atoms present in each of the two bifunctional monomers, and a check on the repeating unit confirms it : \(\mathrm{CO-(CH_2)_4-CO}\) carries six carbon atoms from the acid and \(\mathrm{NH-(CH_2)_6-NH}\) six from the diamine.

stem: Write chemical reaction for the preparation of polyacrylonitrile.
solution:
Polyacrylonitrile is prepared by the **addition polymerization** of acrylonitrile, that is vinyl cyanide \(\mathrm{CH_2{=}CH-CN}\), using a **peroxide initiator** :

\(n\,\mathrm{CH_2{=}CH-CN} \xrightarrow[\text{peroxide}]{\text{polymerization}} \mathrm{[CH_2-CH(CN)]_n}\)

The monomer carries a \(\mathrm{C{=}C}\) double bond, which is what allows it to add : the peroxide supplies a free radical, that radical opens the double bond and the chain grows by successive addition of monomer molecules. Nothing is eliminated, so the repeating unit \(\mathrm{-CH_2-CH(CN)-}\) has the same elemental composition as acrylonitrile itself, which is the mark of an addition polymer.

The \(\mathrm{-CN}\) group remains as a pendant substituent on the backbone and is not part of the chain, so the polymer is linear.

Polyacrylonitrile resembles wool and is used as a wool substitute and for making **Orlon** and **Acrilan**.

stem: Bakelite is the polymer of _____.
solution:
**(C)** Formaldehyde and phenol

Bakelite is the oldest synthetic polymer and is the **thermosetting phenol-formaldehyde** resin, so its two raw materials are phenol \(\mathrm{C_6H_5OH}\) and formaldehyde \(\mathrm{HCHO}\). It is formed in three stages.

**Stage 1.** Phenol and formaldehyde react in presence of an acid or a base catalyst. Formaldehyde attacks the ring at the ortho and para positions, which the \(\mathrm{-OH}\) group activates, giving the hydroxymethyl phenols :

\(\mathrm{C_6H_5OH} + \mathrm{HCHO} \xrightarrow{\text{acid or base}} \mathrm{HO-C_6H_4-CH_2OH}\)

**Stage 2.** These condense with one another, losing water at each step, and the phenol rings become linked through \(\mathrm{-CH_2-}\) bridges to give the linear moulding powder **novolac**.

**Stage 3.** Novolac is placed in a mould and heated at \(138\,^\circ\mathrm{C}\) to \(176\,^\circ\mathrm{C}\) under high pressure. Further \(\mathrm{-CH_2-}\) bridges form at the remaining free ortho and para positions, the chains are cross linked into a rigid three dimensional network, and the insoluble, infusible bakelite is obtained.

Both monomers are necessary and each does a distinct job : phenol supplies the ring with its two activated positions, and formaldehyde supplies the \(\mathrm{-CH_2-}\) bridge that joins one ring to the next. Replacing formaldehyde by a higher aldehyde, or replacing phenol by benzyl alcohol, removes one of the two and the cross linked network cannot be built.

stem: Write names and chemical formulae of monomers used in preparing \(\text{Buna-S}\).
solution:
Buna-S, whose trade name is SBR (styrene-butadiene rubber), is an elastomer which is a **copolymer**, so it is prepared from two different monomers.

| Monomer | Molecular formula | Structural formula |
|---|---|---|
| 1,3-Butadiene | \(\mathrm{C_4H_6}\) | \(\mathrm{CH_2{=}CH-CH{=}CH_2}\) |
| Styrene (vinyl benzene) | \(\mathrm{C_8H_8}\) | \(\mathrm{C_6H_5-CH{=}CH_2}\) |

The copolymer is usually obtained from **75 parts of butadiene and 25 parts of styrene**, subjected to addition polymerization by the action of sodium, and it is vulcanized with sulfur. Both monomers are unsaturated, so each adds without eliminating anything, and the two kinds of repeating unit are randomly sequenced along the chain :

\(\mathrm{{\sim}CH_2-CH{=}CH-CH_2-CH_2-CH{=}CH-CH_2-CH_2-CH(C_6H_5)-CH_2-CH{=}CH-CH_2{\sim}}\)

The name itself records the two monomers and the reagent : **Bu** from butadiene, **Na** from the sodium that brings about the polymerization, and **S** from styrene.

Buna-S is superior to natural rubber in mechanical strength and has abrasion resistance, which is why it is used in the tyre industry.

stem: A polymer used in paints is _____.
solution:
**(D)** glyptal

Glyptal is the polyester obtained from **ethylene glycol and phthalic acid**. The \(\mathrm{-OH}\) groups of the glycol condense with the \(\mathrm{-COOH}\) groups of the acid, water is eliminated and ester linkages are formed, giving the repeating unit

\(\mathrm{[O-CH_2-CH_2-O-CO-C_6H_4-CO]_n}\)

Its commercial application is in **paints and lacquers** : the resin dissolves in the solvent of the paint and, once the solvent has evaporated, sets to a hard, glossy, adhering film.

The other three polymers are not paint resins. Nomex is an aromatic polyamide drawn into a heat-resistant fibre; thiokol is a polysulphide synthetic rubber used for sealants and gaskets; and saran is the vinylidene chloride copolymer extruded as a packaging film. Only the polyester of a glycol and a dibasic acid gives the film-forming resin a paint needs.

stem: Among the following, identify a copolymer.
solution:
**(C)** PHBV

A **copolymer** is a polymer which has two or more types of repeating unit. It is formed by the polymerization of two or more different monomers in presence of each other, and the different monomer units are randomly sequenced in the chain.

PHBV is poly(\(\beta\)-hydroxybutyrate-co-\(\beta\)-hydroxyvalerate). It is the copolymer of **two** bifunctional \(\beta\)-hydroxy carboxylic acids — \(\beta\)-hydroxybutyric acid (3-hydroxybutanoic acid) and \(\beta\)-hydroxyvaleric acid (3-hydroxypentanoic acid). The hydroxyl group of one monomer forms an ester link by reacting with the carboxyl group of the other, so the chain carries two different repeating units and PHBV is an aliphatic polyester copolymer.

Each of the other three is built from a **single** monomer and therefore has only one type of repeating unit, which makes it a homopolymer : orlon is polyacrylonitrile from acrylonitrile, PVC is polyvinyl chloride from vinyl chloride, and teflon is polytetrafluoroethylene from tetrafluoroethylene.

stem: Identify the synthetic polymer among the following.
solution:
**(D)** Terylene

On the basis of **source** polymers are classified as natural, semisynthetic and synthetic. A **synthetic polymer** is a man-made polymer, prepared artificially by the polymerization of one monomer or by the copolymerization of two or more monomers.

Terylene is prepared in exactly that way : it is the polyester obtained by the condensation polymerization of ethylene glycol with terephthalic acid,

\(\mathrm{[O-CH_2-CH_2-O-CO-C_6H_4-CO]_n}\)

so it is a synthetic polymer.

The other three are natural polymers, obtained ready-made from a living source and not built from a monomer in a plant. Linen is the cellulose fibre obtained from the flax plant and jute is likewise a plant fibre, so both are plant polymers; silk is the protein fibre obtained from the silkworm, so it is an animal polymer.

stem: The monomer of natural rubber is _____.
solution:
**(A)** Isoprene

The monomer of natural rubber is **isoprene**, that is 2-methyl-1,3-butadiene :

\(\mathrm{CH_2{=}C(CH_3)-CH{=}CH_2}\)

Natural rubber is a high molecular mass **linear polymer of isoprene**, formed by the addition polymerization of this conjugated diene. Both double bonds take part and a new double bond appears between the middle two carbon atoms of every repeating unit :

\(n\,\mathrm{CH_2{=}C(CH_3)-CH{=}CH_2} \xrightarrow{\text{polymerization}} \mathrm{-[CH_2-C(CH_3){=}CH-CH_2]_n-}\)

The repeating unit is the check : it carries a methyl branch and one double bond in every four carbon atoms, which is exactly what a molecule of isoprene supplies. That surviving double bond is also what allows natural rubber to be vulcanized, and the \(\mathrm{C{=}C}\) bond has the cis configuration, which gives the chain its coiled shape.

The remaining three are the monomers of other polymers : acrylonitrile gives orlon, \(\varepsilon\)-caprolactam gives nylon 6 and tetrafluoroethylene gives teflon.

stem: The monomer used in preparation of teflon is _____.
solution:
**(D)** tetrafluoroethene

Chemically teflon is polytetrafluoroethylene, and the monomer used in its preparation is **tetrafluoroethene** (tetrafluoroethylene), \(\mathrm{CF_2{=}CF_2}\), which is a gas at room temperature.

It is polymerized at high pressure using free radical initiators such as hydrogen peroxide or ammonium persulphate. The monomer is unsaturated, so it adds and no small molecule is eliminated :

\(n\,\mathrm{CF_2{=}CF_2} \xrightarrow[\text{high pressure}]{\text{peroxide}} \mathrm{[CF_2-CF_2]_n}\)

The name of the polymer names its own monomer, and the repeating unit \(\mathrm{-CF_2-CF_2-}\) has the same elemental composition as \(\mathrm{CF_2{=}CF_2}\), which confirms the identification. Every carbon of the chain carries two fluorine atoms, and since the C-F bond is very difficult to break the polymer remains unaffected by corrosive alkali and organic solvents — which is why teflon is used for non-stick cookware, oil seals and gaskets.

The remaining three are the monomers of other polymers : \(\varepsilon\)-caprolactum gives nylon 6, vinyl chloride gives PVC and styrene gives polystyrene.

stem: Write the structure and name of monomer of (a) \(\text{Nylon-6}\) (b) Natural rubber.
solution:
**(a) Nylon 6.**

Monomer : \(\varepsilon\)-caprolactam.

It is the **cyclic amide**, or lactam, formed when the \(\mathrm{-NH_2}\) and \(\mathrm{-COOH}\) groups of \(\varepsilon\)-amino caproic acid react intramolecularly with loss of water. Its structure is the seven membered ring

\(\mathrm{-NH-CO-(CH_2)_5-}\)

whose two open ends, the \(\mathrm{-NH-}\) and the last \(\mathrm{-CH_2-}\), are joined to close the ring. The ring contains one nitrogen atom, one carbonyl carbon and five \(\mathrm{CH_2}\) groups, that is **six carbon atoms**, which is why the polymer is called nylon 6.

On heating with water at 533-543 K the ring opens at the amide bond and gives nylon 6, \(\mathrm{[NH-(CH_2)_5-CO]_n}\).

**(b) Natural rubber.**

Monomer : **isoprene**, that is 2-methyl-1,3-butadiene.

\(\mathrm{CH_2{=}C(CH_3)-CH{=}CH_2}\)

On addition polymerization the conjugated diene gives cis-polyisoprene, that is natural rubber, with the repeating unit

\(\mathrm{-[CH_2-C(CH_3){=}CH-CH_2]_n-}\)

The \(\mathrm{C{=}C}\) double bond of the polyisoprene molecule has the **cis** configuration, which gives the chain its coiled structure and leaves only weak van der Waals forces between chains — the reason natural rubber is an elastomer.

stem: Mention the types of polymers formed on the basis of intermolecular forces. Write any two uses of low density polyethylene.
solution:
**Types of polymers on the basis of intermolecular forces.**

The mechanical properties of a polymer — tensile strength, toughness, elasticity — depend on the forces acting between its chains, and on that basis polymers are placed in four classes.

**1. Elastomers.** Weakest intermolecular forces, of the van der Waals type, which permit the coiled chains to be stretched; a few cross links pull the stretched polymer back to its original shape when the force is removed. Examples : vulcanised rubber, Buna-S, Buna-N, neoprene.

**2. Fibres.** Strongest intermolecular forces — hydrogen bonding and strong dipole-dipole attraction — which hold the chains close and regular, so the solid is crystalline, has high tensile strength and can be drawn into threads. Examples : nylon 6,6, terylene.

**3. Thermoplastic polymers.** Moderately strong intermolecular forces, intermediate between those of elastomers and fibres, with no cross linking, so the polymer softens repeatedly on heating and hardens on cooling and can be remoulded. Examples : polythene, polystyrene, polyvinyls.

**4. Thermosetting polymers.** Extensive cross linking by covalent bonds, formed in the mould during the hot setting process, giving a rigid three dimensional network; once hardened the polymer is infusible and cannot be remoulded. Examples : bakelite, urea-formaldehyde resin.

**Two uses of low density polyethylene.**

1. In the preparation of **pipes** for agriculture, irrigation and domestic water line connections.

2. As **insulation for electric cables**, including submarine cable insulation.

Both uses follow from its properties : LDP films are extremely flexible but tough, chemically inert and moisture resistant, and LDP is a poor conductor of electricity, which is what suits it to carrying water and to covering a live cable.
